Subject: DPA + subprocessors + signing method

Hi Marissa —

We are kicking off contract review on our side for the integration with Redwood. Procurement asked me to request a copy of your standard DPA and your current subprocessor register. Two quick follow-ups for legal:

- Can you confirm the data transfer mechanism you rely on for EU->US processing (SCCs / adequacy / other)?
- Does your hosted product allow EU-only hosting for an enterprise deployment or is that only available with the private deployment?
- Our procurement prefers AdobeSign but we can accept DocuSign if needed. Which is easier on your side?

If possible, please send across your DPA/template so our counsel can start review. We have a soft target to finish legal by end of next week.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: DPA + subprocessors + signing method

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the note. Looping in Ben (Sales Ops) and Lauren (Legal Ops lead) to keep procurement in the loop.

Attached is our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.pdf) and the current subprocessor register (subprocessor_register_20270114.xlsx). Quick answers up front:

- Transfer mechanism: we use the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (EU SCCs) for hosted customers by default and are prepared to add SCCs into the DPA where required. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can keep data residency in EU-only regions.
- Hosting: EU-only hosting is available but requires an integration path (Dedicated or Private). Our hosted public API may route across regions for availability unless you opt into an EU-only tenancy.
- E-sign: we support DocuSign and AdobeSign for DPA execution; our automated workflow currently favors DocuSign but we can accept AdobeSign. If Proc prefers AdobeSign, we will accommodate.

Next steps I recommend: 1) Your counsel can redline the attached DPA and return; 2) We’ll produce a short redline-response matrix and route to our legal team (Lauren & Mina) for approval; 3) Confirm e-sign preference and whether you want SCCs embedded vs. appended.

I’ll stand by for your redline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.pdf]

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Our counsel has redlined the DPA and attached the tracked-document (Finovate_Redlines_v1.docx). High-level comments:

- Narrow the subprocessor approval: we prefer a notice-and-objection flow (14 days) rather than blanket acceptance.
- Add SOC 2 Type II attestation clause or ability to request certs on an annual basis.
- Clarify the liability cap carve-outs for regulatory fines — counsel requests narrower language tied to data processing obligations.
- Please confirm you will include EU SCCs as Exhibit A (we would prefer SCCs appended to the DPA rather than referenced by policy).

Procurement confirms AdobeSign is preferred. If that’s a blocker for you, let me know. We can also insert a short mutual escalation path if Redwood needs more time to review redlines.

Attached: Finovate_Redlines_v1.docx

Sanjay
